question: Should I treat a failed experiment as wasted time?

note.title: When a failed experiment is wasted
note.text:
# When a failed experiment is wasted

A failed experiment can waste time when it repeats a known test, records no result, and changes no future decision. Failure alone is not the waste; running an experiment that cannot reduce uncertainty is.

question: Should I treat a failed experiment as wasted time?

note.title: Failure can buy information
note.text:
# Failure can buy information

A failed experiment is not wasted time when it eliminates a plausible option, exposes a faulty assumption, or improves the next test. The useful output is reduced uncertainty, not a positive result.

note.title: Pre-register the learning condition
note.text:
# Pre-register the learning condition

Before an experiment, write down the expected result, the decision it will inform, and what outcome would change your mind. This makes later interpretation less vulnerable to hindsight.
